_comment: REMOVE THIS MEMBER BEFORE USE — the configuration schema is closed and will refuse it. Copy this file, fill in the keys from your bootstrap ceremony, and keep it out of version control if your caller tokens are not already hashed elsewhere. It holds no secrets: caller credentials appear only as SHA-256 hashes of their bearer tokens, and the only key material referenced is a path to a file the kernel refuses to read unless it is mode 0600.
_comment-notifications: REMOVE THIS MEMBER TOO. The approver ping is the only outbound Stozher owns (ADR-0002) and there are exactly three channels; a fourth is refused at startup, as is a misspelled member inside one. Every credential is named by the environment variable that holds it and is never written here. Zero channels is a legitimate deployment — one operator watching the console — and the pending page says so in words rather than rendering an empty column that reads like 'delivered'. The smtp channel speaks plain SMTP to a relay: with no credential that is the strongest form of 'no plaintext secrets', because there is no secret. If username and password-env are set, it sends AUTH PLAIN only to a loopback relay and refuses otherwise rather than putting a password on the wire in the clear.
